known.title: Decision 7 now needs a lookup in the Codex plugin cache and a blocked result for a changed reviewer copy, but trusted_wrappers stays done and no planned step implements the change, while the wrappers still fall back to the project-local copy
known.locator: Research, Decisions, decision 7 (line 46); Steps, row 9 trusted_wrappers, Status and Done when (line 71)
known.summary: The repair changes decision 7: the Codex wrappers and their templates look up the installed plugin in the Codex plugin cache, and when no installed copy is found they use the project-local agent only when the review input does not change the reviewer files, else they return `blocked`. Step 9 trusted_wrappers keeps the status `done` and its old Done when (installed agent first, project-local only as the fallback), and no new planned step covers the change. At repo_ref, .codex/agents/code-reviewer.toml lines 8-11 load the installed plugin first and use the project-local copy whenever no installed plugin exists, with no cache location and no blocked result, so a diff that changes the reviewer files still sets its own rules when the lookup fails. The plan contract (Repairs, plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/references/plan-contract.md) requires a new step when a decision changes done work. The plan needs a planned step for both wrappers, both templates, and the plan-workspace content hash, with a Done when that checks the lookup and the refusal.

known.title: Step contract_sync changes the contract sentence that code reviewers read after the deciding runs, so C1 ships with a rule that the benchmark did not measure, and Acceptance a6 does not cover the contract
known.locator: Goal (line 5); Steps, row 10 contract_sync (line 72); Acceptance, a6 (line 83)
known.summary: The Goal ships only what the benchmark shows helps. The new step 10 contract_sync changes the plan contract sentence for code reviewers to match C1, and it depends only on step 6 ship, after the deciding runs of step 5. At repo_ref, prepare.mjs (lines 260-265 and 393-398) gives a contract copy only to plan-reviewer variants with a contract overlay; a code arm reads the contract of the case snapshot, so the held-out runs measured C1 with the old sentence 'Code reviewers treat a recorded decision as settled'. results.md line 575 records the same mismatch for the plan #109 candidates. So the shipped code reviewer is C1 plus a contract rule that no run measured. Acceptance a6 compares only the reviewer files of the candidate ref with HEAD, so it does not show the change. The plan must measure C1 with the changed contract under decision 5, or not change the contract.

protected.summary: Yolo decision: this plan does not test a second model family, the external-behavior check (D2), a coverage verdict for unread hunks, web search for the code reviewer, numeric confidence scores, finding caps, or majority votes.

Yolo decision: the dev check runs main and P1 on 6 dev plan cases with 2 runs, and B3 and C3 on 4 dev code cases with 1 run; each candidate may be revised once from the dev check, without held-out data.
Yolo decision: this plan makes no release; plan-lifecycle is released after the merge only with its own question.

Yolo decision: the case builder draws the seed kinds in proportion to the real miss clusters of the published cases, not from the change lists of the candidates; the real *-111-* cases get a separate result that does not decide.
